title: claude-kit project config (v2)
description: Identity layer of a kit project. Resolved in cascade workspace -> project -> island by scripts/lib/kit-config-resolve.sh; the nearest layer wins. The $schema reference in kit.config.json points here so editors validate + autocomplete.

kitVersion.description: Kit version that last wrote/wired this config. Drives self-heal: when it differs from the installed plugin, kit-wire re-converges.

adapters.description: Agent adapters this project installs, written by `cckit init --adapter <claude|codex|both>`. Absent means ["claude"]. `cckit init --upgrade` keeps the stored selection; `--upgrade --adapter <name>` adds one and never removes one.

mode.description: How strict the kit is HERE. draft = guardrails off (explore freely); guided = warnings, never block; enforced = guardrails block (worktree-only, PR-per-issue). Set per cascade level — an island can be enforced while its parent workspace is guided.

workspace.description: Present only in kit.workspace.json (the workspace-root marker). Holds settings shared across every project under the workspace.

commons.description: Path (relative to the workspace root) of the promoted skills/agents commons. Default .claude/.

language.description: Comms language, e.g. en, es, mixed.

path.description: Deprecated: no longer written by cckit init. It held an absolute machine path and nothing reads it; delete it from a config that still has it.

profile.description: Active role profile (minimal, software, content, research, automation, ...).

skillPrefix.description: Namespace prepended to kit-namespaced workflow skills on scaffold/upgrade (e.g. "kit-" -> kit-task-close). Empty = bare names. See templates/skills/NAMESPACED.

modules.description: Stackable modules added on top of the profile (e.g. "software", "qa"). Empty/absent = base project.

qa.description: How THIS project's review stack boots, written by `kit-add.sh qa` from the QA interview (modules/qa.json). cckit records the answers; it does not boot the project by guessing and does not write a boot script. Credentials appear by env var NAME only — a value is refused at interview time and never stored.

command.description: The command that boots the whole review stack (every service a reviewer needs), run from the worktree root, e.g. "pnpm dev:stack".

ports.description: The port env vars the stack command honours, one entry per service. A lane sets each `env` to a port derived from its `base`, so two lanes never share a port. Every base must sit inside ONE `worktree.devPortStride`-wide window, the same invariant as `worktree.devPorts`.

env.description: Env var NAME the stack command reads its port from (e.g. WEB_PORT).

base.description: Base port for this service. The interview derives 3000 + position when the answer names no port.

readiness.description: Readiness probes, one per service that must answer before the stack counts as usable (e.g. web AND API).

env.description: Which service to probe, named by its port env var from `qa.ports`.

path.description: Path requested on that port (e.g. "/" or "/health").

route.description: Route a reviewer lands on when the work declares none (e.g. "/dashboard").

credentialEnv.description: NAMES of the env vars that hold the test account's credentials (e.g. ["QA_EMAIL", "QA_PASSWORD"]). Names only: the values stay in the reviewer's environment.

baseBranch.description: Integration branch the lifecycle skills branch from and merge into (default: main; e.g. develop).

integrationBranch.description: Alias for baseBranch, honored when baseBranch is unset (adoption fallback).

flow.description: Last-resort alias for the integration branch, honored when baseBranch and integrationBranch are unset.

projectOwnerType.description: Whether the Projects v2 board is owned by a user or an organization login (default: user). Selects the GraphQL root for board queries.

tasks.description: Light tasks (`cckit task`): work tracked in the project and not in GitHub issues.

source.description: The task source `cckit task` and `cckit gc` read. `file` (default, the one source shipped): one tracked file per task under `tasks.dir`. Another name loads `scripts/lib/task-source-<name>.sh`, which must define `task_<name>_list`, `_get`, `_create`, `_on_start`, `_on_finish` and `_state`. KIT_TASKS_SOURCE overrides it per invocation.

default.description: Which task list is this project's default. issues (default): GitHub issues, through `cckit new` / `cckit start` / `cckit pr`. light: the `cckit task` list. With light, a bare `cckit next` prints what `cckit task next` prints, and the campaign skill records a campaign's pieces as light tasks instead of sub-issues. Both lists stay usable whatever the value. `cckit task default` prints it. The marketing profile sets light.

check.description: The gate `cckit task run <id>` runs after the agent's round when no `--check` flag is given: a shell command run in the task's worktree. Exit 0 lets the pull request open; any other exit stops the run with exit 6 and opens none. Absent: no gate. The nextjs-shadcn recipe writes `pnpm build && pnpm lint`.

dir.description: The tracked directory the `file` source keeps one `<id>.md` per task in, relative to the project root. An absolute path, or one that climbs out of the project, is ignored with a warning. KIT_TASKS_DIR overrides it per invocation.

enabled.description: Plain language mode. `cckit init` installs the `plain-language` rule while this is true: the agent says draft, review and approve, and names worktree, branch and pull request only when asked. `cckit task` words its progress lines the same way (its `--llm` output and its stdout are unchanged). The marketing profile turns it on; `cckit init --plain-language on|off` sets it for any profile. On `--upgrade` the stored value wins over the profile default.

content.description: When true, `scripts/setup-labels.sh` (and the label step of `cckit init`) provisions the content kind labels `kind:post`, `kind:campaign`, `kind:brand` and `kind:research`. The content and marketing profiles set it. The kinds are accepted by `--kind` with or without this key: a content kind starts on a branch prefix from the closed set (post and brand: `task/`, campaign: `plan/`, research: `spike/`) and titles its PR `docs:`.

titleStyle.description: How `cckit pr` titles a single-issue PR. conventional (default): a Conventional Commits subject derived from the kind label, which release-please and a commitlint gate read. issue-title: the issue title, verbatim. `cckit effort pr` follows the same key: conventional gives `type(scope): name [#N]` and refuses a title that fails commitlint; issue-title gives `[Role] [#N] name`, unchecked.

bodyStyle.description: The wording of the PR body `cckit pr`, `cckit effort pr` and `cckit task finish` generate. code (default): a Verification checklist that names the diff. content: a Review checklist for a draft (read it through, facts and links checked, voice matches the brand guide, only the files for this piece changed). `Closes #N`, the summary and the role signature are the same in both. The content and marketing profiles set content.

orchestratorSection.description: When true, `cckit pr` opens the PR body with a two-line `## For the orchestrator` section: the issue number and what to review.

flows.description: Controlled flow vocabulary for effort titles — the values accepted by the leading [Flow] title tag and `--flow` (also the flow:<flow> labels). Replaces the built-in default (Core UI API Docs Infra Auth Data Web App); an explicit EFFORT_FLOWS env var still wins per invocation.

preCloseHook.description: Optional path to an executable `cckit effort close` runs BEFORE the snapshot and the merge, invoked as `<hook> <effort-number> <sub-number>…` with cwd = the effort worktree (wave-style close: the checkout the close was run from). A relative path resolves against the main checkout. A non-zero exit refuses the close with nothing written; so does a configured hook that is missing or not executable. `KIT_FORCE=1` skips the hook and says so. An explicit KIT_EFFORT_PRE_CLOSE_HOOK env var wins per invocation. No-op when unset; the kit ships no default.

knowledgeIngestHook.description: Optional path to an executable run after `cckit effort close`, invoked as `<hook> <effort-number> <trace-dir>` to fold the closed effort's work record into a knowledge base. No-op when unset or not executable; the kit ships no default.

planSource.description: Optional path to an executable `cckit effort plan` calls for the open-effort rows instead of querying GitHub, invoked as `<source> <owner/repo>` from the project root (a relative path resolves against that root). It prints one `number<TAB>flow<TAB>ctx<TAB>title[<TAB>blockers]` line per open effort, `blockers` being a comma-separated list of issue numbers, and may print a `# age: <text>` line saying how old its data is. The plan prints which source it used, with that age. A source that is not executable, exits non-zero or prints no rows falls back to GitHub, and the plan says so. Unset: GitHub is read. An explicit EFFORT_PLAN_SOURCE env var wins per invocation.

wipLimit.description: How many efforts may be in progress at once before `cckit effort start` refuses a NEW effort (default 2). In progress = an `effort/<N>-<slug>` branch exists as a local head or on origin (read with `git ls-remote`, not the cached refs/remotes; EFFORT_WIP_REMOTE=0 or an unreachable origin counts the cached refs instead). Refusal happens before anything is written; `--force` (or KIT_FORCE=1) starts anyway. 0 refuses every ordinary start of a NEW effort but not a forced one, and not a re-start of an effort already in progress (that adds no WIP, so it is never gated); a non-integer value is ignored with a warning and the default is used. An explicit EFFORT_WIP_LIMIT env var wins per invocation. Does not affect `cckit start <issue>`.

model.description: Which environment variables the hosted effort-metrics judge reads. Names only, never values — no URL or token belongs in this file. Every key is optional; unset, the built-in name is used. A value that is not a shell identifier (letters, digits, underscore, not starting with a digit) is ignored with a warning and the built-in name is used.

urlEnv.description: Env var holding the OpenAI-compatible base URL; the judge POSTs to `<value>/chat/completions`. Empty or unset at run time: the hosted judge is skipped and the local model (if enabled) is tried.

modelEnv.description: Env var holding the model name sent in the request and recorded as the record's judge model id. Empty or unset at run time: the literal `default` is sent.

tokenEnv.description: Env var holding the bearer token. Empty or unset at run time: no Authorization header is sent.

night.description: Night mode (`kit-autopilot` § Mode: night): what `scripts/night-grant.sh` adds to the owner's night grant before it launches `scripts/night-run.mjs`. Every key is optional; without the object a night run uses the base floors, the delegation brief's gate, and accepts a grant only from `github.owner` or a commenter GitHub reports as OWNER.

floors.description: Extra always-human floors, name -> what a diff must touch to trip it. Added to the base floors (lockfile, auth, security-code, security-prose, workflows, cost, secret). A tripped floor parks the effort unless that night's grant waives it by its exact name.

neverWaivable.description: Floor names no grant may waive, added to the base list (workflows, cost, secret). A grant that waives one is refused when it is read; the engine refuses it again at merge time.

gate.description: The gate command executors and verifiers run, and the command the final check runs on the base branch once every wave merged. Unset: the gate commands in the project's delegation brief.

grantors.description: GitHub logins allowed to write the night grant, besides `github.owner` and any commenter whose author_association is OWNER. Compared case-insensitively. Needed on an organization repo, where no commenter is OWNER and `github.owner` is the org. A grant comment from any other author is ignored.

refuseLabels.description: Labels that hold an effort out of a night run: preflight refuses an effort carrying any of them. Default: none. The kit applies no such label itself.

agents.description: Named agent profiles and the stage vocabulary they are allowed at. A profile declares a SPEND POSTURE (`tier`) and the CLI arguments to run (`args`) — cckit never names a model, so it cannot push you onto an expensive one. Resolution precedence is command override > issue metadata > parent effort metadata > `agents.default` (see `cckit effort`/orchestration docs).

default.description: Profile name used when nothing more specific resolves. Must name a key of `agents.profiles`; a `default` that names no declared profile is a validation error, not a silent fallback. OMIT IT to get the lowest-tier declared profile, which is the recommended setting: naming an expensive profile here makes every unlabelled issue expensive.

stages.description: Controlled stage vocabulary a profile's `stages` entries are checked against. Replaces the built-in default (build review design docs); an explicit CCKIT_AGENT_STAGES env var wins per invocation.

kind.description: The agent CLI/provider this profile runs, e.g. `claude` or `codex`. Must be a kind the selected runtime can start — the Herdr runtime validates it before any worktree is created.

tier.description: How much this profile is expected to COST to run, relative to the others. cckit never names a model: the spend posture lives here and the actual flags live in `args`. `low` is assumed when unstated, and the lowest-tier profile is what runs when `agents.default` is not set — so the cheap path is the default by construction rather than by discipline.

args.description: Extra CLI arguments appended to the launch command, as an argv array (never a shell string, so nothing is re-parsed by a shell). The project spells its own flags here — including any model selection — so no vendor CLI syntax and no model id lives in kit code.

permissions.description: Permission/sandbox policy this profile runs under, forwarded to the CLI that implements it. Recorded in the stage receipt so a run's effective policy is auditable after the fact.

stages.description: Stages this profile may run at, each a value from `agents.stages`. A profile selected for a stage it does not list is refused before a worktree or pane exists.

write.description: Whether this profile may write to a branch (default false). One writer owns a branch at a time; review profiles stay read-only until ownership is explicitly transferred.

contextBudget.description: Upper bound, in BYTES, on the whole prompt a worker of this profile receives. Whole `## ` sections are dropped from the end of the brief until it fits, and the prompt then names which ones were dropped and how to read them — a truncated brief must read as truncated. Four things are never dropped: the headless framing, the brief's own metadata (worktree, branch, seed freshness, gate command), the truncation notice itself, and the receipt contract. A budget too small to hold those emits them anyway and warns on stderr, because a worker with no receipt contract reports in a shape nothing can parse. Unset, 0, or non-numeric means unbounded. The board and prior conversations are never included at any budget.

profiles.description: Map of profile name to its declaration. Profile names are stable cckit policy referenced by issue and effort metadata; the vendor model id and CLI arguments inside each are project-owned.

floors.description: Auto-merge policy floors (default true). When on, `cckit watch --merge` never auto-merges a PR touching .github/workflows/**, lockfile/graph files, or security-sensitive paths, and always honors a `hold` label + draft state. Set false to disable (or KIT_CAPTAIN_FLOORS=0).

protectedGlobs.description: Extra path globs the captain must not auto-merge (added to the built-in floors). Also settable via KIT_CAPTAIN_EXTRA_GLOBS.

requireQa.description: Hold a PR for a human QA pass (default false). true: `cckit watch --merge` reads every would-be merge with no `cckit qa verdict pass` recorded against its current head as QA_MISSING (action verify). A list of label names: only PRs carrying one of them, e.g. ["flow:ui"]. A recorded QA fail on the current head blocks regardless (QA_FAILING). Env: KIT_CAPTAIN_REQUIRE_QA=1|0, KIT_CAPTAIN_QA_LABELS (space-separated); either one set means the key is not read.

local.description: Local model layer: natural-language chores run on this machine through mlx_lm.server. Off when absent. `enabled` is the config key of the integration descriptor integrations/mlx-lm.json.

enabled.description: true = `cckit doctor` installs the runtime (with consent) and starts the server.

model.description: Model the server loads. Default mlx-community/Qwen3-8B-4bit.

dismissed.description: kitVersion at which the "local layer down" session notice was dismissed (`cckit doctor --dismiss-local`).

codeGraph.description: Code-graph retrieval: agents query an index of the code instead of grepping the tree. Off when absent. Turned on by an integration descriptor (integrations/<id>.json) whose `config.key` is `codeGraph.provider`.

provider.description: Which integration provides the code graph, as the descriptor's `config.value` names it. Absent or "none" = no code graph; every path that would use one skips.

reviewPages.description: Review pages: a plan, a decision with options or a grilling round opens as an HTML page the reader annotates and answers (`cckit page`). ON when absent. `enabled` is the config key of the integration descriptor integrations/lavish.json, which is on by default.

enabled.description: false = plans, decisions and grills print to the terminal; `cckit page open` never starts the page tool. Absent or true = a page opens in a session that has a browser.

answers.description: Where `cckit page answer` writes. Absent = a comment on the issue when `github.repo` is set and `--issue` is given, else a file. `issue` requires `--issue`; `file` always writes a file.

answersDir.description: Directory, relative to the repo root, for answers written as files. Default `docs/answers`. A path that leaves the repo is refused.

routines.description: Opt-in scheduled routines accepted by the user (briefing, board sweep, gc, ...). The kit SUGGESTS; the user accepts; nothing is created without opt-in.

upgrade.description: Tells `init.sh --upgrade` which scaffolded paths the project deleted/renamed ON PURPOSE so they are never re-added (#334). Paths are repo-relative (e.g. ".claude/skills/task-new"); a directory entry covers everything beneath it.

removed.description: Scaffolded paths the project deleted on purpose — the upgrade will not re-create them.

renamed.description: Map of original scaffolded path -> the project's new name. The original (key) is treated as removed (never re-added); the value documents where it went.

worktree.description: How `cckit start` / `cckit effort start` bootstrap a fresh worktree (env copy, dev port, dependency install). Every key is optional; the kit hardcodes no project layout.

installPaths.description: Worktree-relative directories to run `pnpm install` in during bootstrap (e.g. ["docs-site"]). Set, it wins outright — only these dirs are installed and the checks below are skipped; [] installs nothing. Entries MUST stay inside the worktree: an absolute path, a `..` that climbs out, or a symlink pointing outside is refused and skipped. Unset: install at the root only when its package.json declares dependencies or it is a workspace root WITH AT LEAST ONE MEMBER — a dependency-free root (or an empty `packages:` / `workspaces` list) is skipped so pnpm cannot plant an empty pnpm-lock.yaml (#255). KIT_WT_INSTALL=0 skips the install entirely.

devPorts.description: Per-app dev PORT lanes. Each entry writes PORT = base + <slot> * <devPortStride> into that app's .env.local, so parallel worktrees never fight for a port. <slot> is ALLOCATED and recorded per issue under the git-common-dir (kit-portslots.tsv), not hashed from the issue number: an issue keeps its slot while its worktree exists, and the slot is reclaimed once that worktree is gone. Best-effort: it only takes effect for an app that actually reads the file. `next dev -p ${PORT:-3003}` is expanded by the npm-script shell, which never reads .env.local, so the value is inert for it. cckit does not rely on this — whatever cckit launches itself receives its port explicitly.

path.description: Repo-relative path to the app's .env.local file.

base.description: Base port for this app's lane. Every app's base must sit inside ONE devPortStride-wide window (e.g. 3001/3003/3004 with stride 10); a wider spread lets two worktrees' blocks overlap, and cckit warns when it sees one.

devPortStride.description: Distance between one worktree's port block and the next (default 10 — room for up to 10 services). It must NOT be the number of services: with stride == count, two bases congruent mod count hand the SAME port to two different worktrees (bases 3001/3003/3004 with count 3 gave worktree slot k+1's admin port to slot k's api). Widen it when a project declares more devPorts entries than the stride, or when its bases span further than one stride.
